paper_metadata.title: Randomized controlled trial of 2.5-cm versus 3.5-cm mesial temporal resection in temporal lobe epilepsy—part 1: intent-to-treat analysis

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the target population, recruitment centers, and inclusion/exclusion criteria. A detailed flowchart accounts for eligible non-participants, and baseline characteristics are well-balanced between groups.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Patients in the three epilepsy surgery centers at the Universities of Bonn, Freiburg, and Berlin were recruited for this study between October 2002 and December 2005.
items.reasoning: The study specifies the clinical setting (tertiary epilepsy centers) and the specific condition (drug-resistant TLE).

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: In each center, patients with temporal lobe epilepsy were screened and evaluated, and if recruited for the study, were followed up by that center.
items.reasoning: The recruitment process within specialized centers is described, and the flowchart shows the screening of 318 cases.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Patients were recruited between mid-October 2002 and end of December 2005.
items.reasoning: Specific dates for the recruitment window are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: three epilepsy surgery centers at the Universities of Bonn, Freiburg, and Berlin
items.reasoning: The geographic and institutional settings are explicitly named.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Patients were eligible for this study if they suffered from drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy and presurgical evaluation had led to the recommendation of either a partial temporal lobe resection combined with amygdalohippocampectomy or a more restricted selected SAH.
items.reasoning: Criteria include age, drug resistance definition, and specific surgical indications.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: A total of 318 cases were assessed for eligibility... 207 patients were allocated to the two intervention types
items.reasoning: The participation rate is high (207/318), and reasons for exclusion (refusal, not meeting criteria) are transparently reported.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Gender distribution, mean age at time of operation, duration of epilepsy, side of surgery, and age at onset of seizure disorder are shown for all analyzed patients
items.reasoning: Table 1 and 2 provide comprehensive baseline data, showing no significant differences between groups.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study achieved 100% follow-up for the primary outcome (seizure freedom at 1 year) for all 207 randomized patients, using an intent-to-treat approach.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Seizure outcome was available for 207 patients, complete volumetric results for 179 patients.
items.reasoning: 100% of the randomized sample was available for the primary outcome analysis.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: The second death (traffic accident) occurred 9 months after the operation, but we have a 7 months' outcome available for him and carried this forward for the primary analysis.
items.reasoning: The study describes how they handled the very few cases of missing data/death to maintain the ITT analysis.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: Two patients died, one randomized to the short group by suicide 13 months after his operation... The second death (traffic accident) occurred 9 months after the operation
items.reasoning: Specific reasons for the only two 'losses' (deaths) are provided.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: one randomized to the short group by suicide 13 months after his operation with outcome Engel I.
items.reasoning: The characteristics and outcomes of the deceased patients are noted.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: The group available for the primary analysis consisted of these 207 cases.
items.reasoning: Since all 207 were analyzed for the primary outcome, there is no attrition bias for the main result.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (intended resection length) was the intervention itself in this RCT. It was clearly defined and verified postoperatively using objective MRI volumetry with high inter-rater reliability.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: one with an intended minimum mesial resection of 25 mm from the tip of the temporal horn backwards and the other one with a mesial minimum resection of 35 mm
items.reasoning: The 'prognostic factor' (resection length) is explicitly defined in millimeters.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: MRI volumetry was done only centrally using an epilepsy-dedicated MRI protocol... intrarater reliability... was calculated with the intraclass correlation coefficient between 0.93 and 0.98
items.reasoning: The use of centralized MRI volumetry with high ICC ensures reliable measurement of the actual resection.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: 2.5-cm versus 3.5-cm mesial temporal resection
items.reasoning: The cut-points were pre-specified by the study design, not derived from the data.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The MRI studies were organized in each center following a common MRI protocol. MRI volumetry was done only centrally
items.reasoning: Standardized protocols and centralized analysis were used for all patients.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: complete volumetric results for 179 patients.
items.reasoning: While 28 patients lacked volumetric data, the primary ITT analysis used the 'intended' group, which was known for all 207.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Outcome analysis was restricted to control of successful randomization and an intent-to-treat analysis of seizure outcome.
items.reasoning: The study used ITT to handle missingness in the primary analysis, though it doesn't explicitly mention imputation for the 179/207 volumetric subgroup.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure freedom) was measured using the standard Engel scale. Assessors were blinded to the resection group, and follow-up intervals were standardized.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Primary outcome measure was seizure freedom at 1 year and during the full first year expressed as class I in the Engel outcome scale.
items.reasoning: The Engel scale is a validated, standard measure in epilepsy surgery.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Neither the study participants nor the epileptologists assessing the outcomes were told of the result of the randomization
items.reasoning: Blinding of both participants and outcome assessors (epileptologists) significantly reduces measurement bias.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: All patients were regularly followed up, the first time at 3 months after surgery, then at 6 months after surgery, and at 1 year after surgery.
items.reasoning: Follow-up schedule was identical for all participants.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: As an RCT, randomization successfully balanced known confounders (age, duration, pathology). Multivariable analysis was not the primary focus, but the balance of baseline characteristics suggests low risk.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: Gender distribution, mean age at time of operation, duration of epilepsy, side of surgery, and age at onset of seizure disorder are shown
items.reasoning: Key prognostic factors in TLE surgery were measured and reported.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: Drug resistance was defined as seizure duration of more than 2 years despite continuous treatment with at least two antiepileptic drugs
items.reasoning: Clinical variables like drug resistance and pathology (MTS) are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: diagnosis and grade of hippocampal sclerosis were reviewed and confirmed by the reference center for histopathology
items.reasoning: Use of a reference center for pathology ensures high reliability of the most important confounder (MTS).

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Presurgical evaluation was harmonized between the centers with all patients having video-EEG recordings, MRI evaluation using the same protocol
items.reasoning: Harmonized protocols across centers ensure consistency.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods are used if imputation is used for missing confounder data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The text does not explicitly discuss missing data for confounders, though Table 1 suggests complete data for the 207 patients.

items.label: Appropriate Accounting for Confounding
items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).
items.evidence_snippet: A computer-generated blocked randomization list was prepared
items.reasoning: Randomization is the gold standard for accounting for both known and unknown confounders.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: The rates were compared using the Fisher's exact test primarily
items.reasoning: The primary analysis was univariable (Fisher's exact). While randomization makes this acceptable, multivariable adjustment was not presented in this 'Part 1' paper.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical plan is well-described, including power calculations and an ITT approach. Results are reported transparently for all randomized patients.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: The rates were compared using the Fisher's exact test primarily for the population of patients who had followed the study protocol... A secondary analysis was performed taking into account all randomized patients (intention-to-treat)
items.reasoning: The strategy for both per-protocol and ITT analyses is clear.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: Sample size was determined to be able to detect the advantage of 80% seizure freedom for one resection type against a rate of seizure freedom of 60%
items.reasoning: The analysis is based on a clear hypothesis-testing framework with a pre-specified power calculation.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: Fisher's exact test primarily for the population of patients
items.reasoning: Fisher's exact test is appropriate for comparing proportions in this study design.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: Seizure outcome classes Engel I –IV were not different for the group with intended 2.5-cm versus intended 3.5-cm resection (Fig. 3).
items.reasoning: The study reports on all randomized patients and provides the full distribution of outcomes (Engel I-IV), not just the 'significant' ones.
